WASHINGTON (TNND) — The FBI failed to thoroughly investigate materials pertaining to its investigation of Hillary Clinton's use of a private email server during her time as Secretary of State.

A whistleblower gave the FBI thumb drives that "contained highly sensitive information exfiltrated from U.S. government agencies, including the Department of State, as well as then-President Barack Obama’s emails and, potentially, congressional information," but the FBI failed to review them, according to declassified materials documents from the "Clinton annex" found in the appendix of a 2018 Department of Justice Office of Inspector General report.
Clinton, who served as Secretary of State in the Obama administration from 2009 to 2013, was under investigation by the FBI for sharing and storing classified materials on a private email server.
The FBI, headed by Director James Comey, advised against seeking criminal charges to Clinton, the Democratic presidential nominee in July 2016 — just months before the presidential election.
